chapter: Own groups, bebop and Savoy sessions
title: Savoy recordings of the 1940s

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay, Cozy, we took a break for a while and we got to talking a little bit about all the recordings you did for Savoy in the '40s. Do you want to talk a little about that?
Yes. Teddy Reig was connected with Savoy label at that time. I did a lot of things for Savoy with a combination trumpet, tenor, and three rhythm, and Lubinsky...

Herman Lubinsky, he was, he was the owner of the label. I just forget all the names, the tunes that we did, but I liked the label very much. It was one of those good old stomp down, drag out labels, you know, where you'd get up there and swing and stomp and go on, and I did quite a few recording dates for Savoy.

There's a re-issue of a lot of those records have been reissued recently. Let's see, they put out an anthology of various tenor players, Ben Webster and his version of 'Body and Soul' that Ben had done and that you had recorded with.
Let me reach for the record. Yeah that was in 1944 and that was with Johnny Guarnieri and Billy Taylor and Teddy Walters.
There was a good guitar player, Teddy Walters.
Yeah, you don't hear very much about him.
No, he was a great little guitar player. Teddy Walters.
Did he play a lot around 52nd Street?
Oh yeah, he was there on 52nd Street with different groups, very good. I used him on several of my recording dates. Teddy Walters.

Let's see what Chilton says happened to him. He's not even listed, that's funny. Also there was a tenor player named John Hardy that you did some records with in '47. Do you remember much about those?

No, I don't remember John. I know him, but my acquaintance with him wasn't real tight you know, but I knew him. I of course like Ben, Don Byas and those boys, I was real close to. But John Hardy I knew. Ike Quebec, I knew very good. But John Hardy I knew but we weren't
